newsitem.title: USA: BankAmerica suit no threat to Calif debt - Treasurer.
newsitem.headline: BankAmerica suit no threat to Calif debt - Treasurer.

text.p: California state Treasurer Matt Fong said on Thursday that San Francisco's lawsuit against BankAmerica Corp would not undermine the "integrity" of state or local municipal bonds.

"Investors who have or are considering buying California bonds need not be concerned that the city of San Francisco's lawsuit will adversely affect the value of California bonds," Fong said in a statement. "I want to eliminate any possible uncertainty over the integrity of our bonds."
San Francisco on Thursday sued BankAmerica, the nation's third-largest bank, alleging it mishandled hundreds of millions of dollars in municipal bond funds and engaged in a massive cover-up.

City Attorney Louise Renne said the lawsuit -- seeking at least $12 million in damages -- alleges the bank, acting as a trustee, mishandled bond funds issued for low-income housing, schools, fire protection and other public works.

BankAmerica said San Francisco's claims were "short on reality." It said its Institutional Trust Department, which it sold in 1995, unintentionally overcharged the city for trust services and retained some funds.
